source.description: Carries each package's source hash to its dependents, so a check reruns when a package it loads changes, without waiting for that package's checks.

typecheck.description: The typecheck, `pnpm types` and `pnpm check`'s: each package's and the root's project checked from scratch by toolchain-typecheck, which reads no build info (TypeScript 7.1.0-beta's incremental check passed an unused import over an earlier version's build info, METIS-BOOT 2026-11-20), so a hit replays the diagnostics of exactly these inputs and a miss checks them whole. It writes nothing, so it has no output. The dev tools' tsconfig bases, which the root tsconfig and every package extend, are inputs too.

oxlint.description: The dev tools' preset and plugin and the repository's config are inputs too.

load.description: Every package's test modules loaded apart, through toolchain-test load: a module whose closure loaded before is a cached answer in toolchain-test's own load cache, keyed by its closure hash, so turbo caches nothing of it.

test.description: Every package's properties, through toolchain-test run. Each run draws a fresh rotating seed, so a run never replays from cache; the run's seed comes through the environment (and the old fuzz script's variables). The PostgreSQL cluster the testing library's database properties need is the package's own (packages/testing/pg.config.ts; CONTRIBUTING.md, "Properties that need a database"), whose members are units of the workbench's postgres@: the harness reads the CA their certificates chain to from PGSSLROOTCERT (pg/settle.ts caVariable) and a member's socket from XDG_RUNTIME_DIR, and a settle starts units over the account's bus (DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS), so those pass through, where turbo's strict environment strips them (trunk@toolchain red at 7c9d754, PGSSLROOTCERT unset).

//#workspace-gate.description: The repository-wide checks: every tsconfig and package manifest, and every file name git shows. It reads the whole tree and opens no TypeScript program, so it costs about a second, and a cache would have to hash the whole tree to know it could skip it.

//#dedupe.description: The lockfile is already deduplicated: pnpm dedupe would change nothing.
